mcq.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: Ali Mardan Khan introduced the system of revenue farming in Bengal
Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up modern foundries to manufacture cannons at Lahore
Sawai Jai Singh of Amber had Euclid's 'Elements of Geometry' translated into Sanskrit
Tipu Sultan of Mysore gave money for the construction of the idol of goddess Sharada in the Sringeri temple
mcq.x: Revenue farming (ijaradari) in Bengal was introduced by Murshid Quli Khan, not Ali Mardan Khan; the other three statements are correct.

mcq.s: In which year was the export of slaves from Bengal banned?
mcq.x: The export of slaves from Bengal was banned in 1789 under Cornwallis; slavery itself was declared illegal in India in 1843 (Act V of 1843).

why: answer not certain (share of central revenue spent on the army)

mcq.s: Who among the following fought against the British in the Revolt of 1857?
mcq.x: Saadat Khan led the rising of Holkar's troops at Indore in 1857; the other three belong to the 20th-century freedom struggle.

mcq.s: Match List-I (Centre of the Revolt of 1857) with List-II (Leader): A. Jhansi B. Lucknow C. Kanpur D. Faizabad; 1. Maulvi Ahmad Shah 2. Azimullah Khan 3. Begum Hazrat Mahal 4. Rani Lakshmibai
mcq.x: Rani Lakshmibai led at Jhansi, Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow, Azimullah Khan (with Nana Saheb) at Kanpur and Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah at Faizabad.

mcq.s: Arrange the following revolts in chronological order: 1. Pabna 2. Indigo 3. Kuka 4. Sanyasi
mcq.x: Sanyasi Revolt (1763-1800), Indigo Revolt (1859-60), Kuka Revolt (1871-72), Pabna peasant movement (1873-76).

mcq.s: Who founded the 'Pagal Panth' sect, whose followers led the Pagal Panthi rising?
mcq.x: The Pagal Panth, a semi-religious sect of North Bengal, was founded by Karam (Karim) Shah; his son Tipu Shah led the Garo peasants' rising (1825-33).

mcq.s: The Kol uprising of 1831-32 under Buddho Bhagat took place in which region?
mcq.x: The Kols of Chhotanagpur (Ranchi, Singhbhum, Hazaribagh, Palamau, Manbhum) rose in 1831-32 under Buddho Bhagat against outsiders brought in by British land laws.

mcq.s: The Waghera uprising (1818-20) took place in the territory of:
mcq.x: The Wagheras of Okhamandal rose (1818-20) against the Gaekwad of Baroda, who was backed by the British. The printed key (Surat) is wrong.

why: answer not certain (date of the Chhotanagpur tribal revolt is ambiguous)

o: High interest rates charged by moneylenders (Mahajans)
Protest against the imposition of new taxes

mcq.s: Which of the following popular papers of the revolutionary period criticised the Congress for various reasons?
mcq.x: Bangabasi, Kaal and Kesari were all popular papers of the period that criticised the Congress and its moderate policies.

mcq.s: Match List-I (Paper) with List-II (Person): A. Samachar Darpan B. Mirat-ul-Akhbar C. Kesari D. Young India; 1. Raja Ram Mohan Roy 2. B.G. Tilak 3. Mahatma Gandhi 4. J.C. Marshman
mcq.x: Samachar Darpan – J.C. Marshman (Serampore); Mirat-ul-Akhbar – Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Kesari – Tilak; Young India – Gandhi.

why: Uttar Pradesh local journalism (places of publication)

mcq.s: Which is the correct order of the editors of The Hindu, Kesari, The Bengalee, Hindustani and Sudharak respectively?
o: Surendranath Banerjee, G. Subramania Iyer, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Ganga Prasad Varma
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, G. Subramania Iyer, Surendranath Banerjee, Ganga Prasad Varma, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
G. Subramania Iyer, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Ganga Prasad Varma, Surendranath Banerjee, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
G. Subramania Iyer, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Surendranath Banerjee, Ganga Prasad Varma, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
mcq.x: The Hindu – G. Subramania Iyer; Kesari – Tilak; The Bengalee – Surendranath Banerjee; Hindustani – Ganga Prasad Varma; Sudharak – G.K. Gokhale (with Agarkar).

mcq.s: Match List-I (Organisation) with List-II (Person): 1. Prarthana Samaj 2. Brahmo Samaj 3. Arya Samaj 4. Ramakrishna Mission; A. Raja Ram Mohan Roy B. Vivekananda C. Dayanand Saraswati D. M.G. Ranade E. Ramakrishna Paramhansa
mcq.x: Prarthana Samaj – M.G. Ranade (its leading member; founded by Atmaram Pandurang); Brahmo Samaj – Ram Mohan Roy; Arya Samaj – Dayanand Saraswati; Ramakrishna Mission – Vivekananda (1897).

mcq.s: Match List-I (Society) with List-II (Founder): A. Brahmo Samaj B. Ramakrishna Mission C. Servants of India Society D. Vidhva Vivah Samaj; i. Vishnu Shastri Pandit ii. Swami Vivekananda iii. Raja Ram Mohan Roy iv. Gopal Krishna Gokhale
mcq.x: Brahmo Samaj – Ram Mohan Roy; Ramakrishna Mission – Vivekananda; Servants of India Society – Gokhale (1905); Widow Remarriage Society – Vishnu Shastri Pandit.

mcq.s: Match List-I with List-II: A. Servants of India Society B. Tattvabodhini Sabha C. Atmiya Sabha; 1. Debendranath Tagore 2. Gopal Krishna Gokhale 3. Raja Ram Mohan Roy 4. Keshab Chandra Sen
mcq.x: Servants of India Society – Gokhale (1905); Tattvabodhini Sabha – Debendranath Tagore (1839); Atmiya Sabha – Ram Mohan Roy (1815).

mcq.s: Which is the correct combination of persons associated with Prarthana Samaj, Young India, Lokahitavadi, Satyashodhak Samaj and Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha respectively?
o: Gopal Hari Deshmukh, Atmaram Pandurang, M.K. Gandhi, Jyotiba Phule, Naoroji Furdonji
Atmaram Pandurang, M.K. Gandhi, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, Jyotiba Phule, Naoroji Furdonji
Atmaram Pandurang, Jyotiba Phule, M.K. Gandhi, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, Naoroji Furdonji
Naoroji Furdonji, Atmaram Pandurang, M.K. Gandhi, Jyotiba Phule, Gopal Hari Deshmukh
mcq.x: Prarthana Samaj – Atmaram Pandurang (1867); Young India – Gandhi; 'Lokahitavadi' – Gopal Hari Deshmukh; Satyashodhak Samaj – Jyotiba Phule (1873); Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha – Naoroji Furdonji and others (1851).

mcq.s: Consider the following statements: 1. Brahmo Samaj supported monotheism. 2. Arya Samaj contributed to the development of education. 3. Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission. Which of these are true?
mcq.x: All three are true: the Brahmo Samaj preached worship of one God, the Arya Samaj ran DAV schools and gurukuls, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

mcq.s: The Tarkeswar Movement of 1924 in Bengal was against:
mcq.x: The Tarkeswar Satyagraha (1924) was against the corrupt and immoral mahant of the Tarkeswar Shiva temple in Bengal.

mcq.s: The 'Hali system' was concerned with:
mcq.x: Hali was a system of hereditary bonded labour in Gujarat (notably the Bardoli area), under which the Halis worked for upper-caste landlords to pay off debts.

mcq.s: In which year was Surendranath Banerjee dismissed from the Indian Civil Service?
mcq.x: Selected in 1869, Surendranath Banerjee was dismissed from the ICS in 1874 on a minor procedural ground.

mcq.s: Match List-I (Association) with List-II (Leader): A. Indian Association B. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha C. Bombay Presidency Association D. Madras Mahajana Sabha; 1. Pherozeshah Mehta 2. Surendranath Banerjee 3. P. Ananda Charlu 4. M.G. Ranade
mcq.x: Indian Association – Surendranath Banerjee (1876); Poona Sarvajanik Sabha – M.G. Ranade; Bombay Presidency Association – Pherozeshah Mehta (1885); Madras Mahajana Sabha – P. Ananda Charlu and others (1884).

mcq.s: A future Governor-General of India attended a session of the Indian National Congress. Identify him and the place of the session.
mcq.x: Lord Willingdon, then Governor of Bombay, attended the Bombay session of 1915; he was Viceroy and Governor-General in 1931-36.

mcq.s: Match List-I (Place of a Congress session in Uttar Pradesh) with List-II (Year): A. Meerut B. Kanpur C. Lucknow D. Banaras; 1. 1916 2. 1905 3. 1946 4. 1925
mcq.x: Meerut 1946 (J.B. Kripalani), Kanpur 1925 (Sarojini Naidu), Lucknow 1916 (A.C. Majumdar) and Banaras 1905 (G.K. Gokhale).

why: answer not certain (founders of the Hindustan Socialist Democratic Union)
